depth_history.shortcut_targeted: The equivalence between safe two-mode assignments and bipartite coloring of the warning graph.
depth_history.edit_summary: No semantics-preserving edit can defeat all survivors because bipartite coloring is the core task. If changing the task is allowed, add a mutable global constraint such as requiring exactly half the machines in each mode; this preserves the given examples but invalidates ordinary component-wise coloring solutions.

depth_history.shortcut_targeted: The product constraint on binary factors is exactly the condition that every critical-link edge joins opposite colors, reducing the task to bipartite graph testing and coloring.
depth_history.edit_summary: Replace the explicit sentence "the calibration factors of the two machines in any critical link must multiply to exactly 2" with an indirect, scenario-defined compatibility/state-transition rule that has the same accepted endpoint assignments but does not reveal the two-color interpretation syntactically.

resistant_to: Models warnings as undirected edges and uses BFS parity coloring.
Treats factors 1 and 2 as two colors and performs BFS bipartite checking.
Uses connected-component BFS with temporary binary colors, then chooses the lexicographically better orientation.
Uses a 0/1 color array and BFS over each connected component, then maps colors to factors 1/2.
Uses BFS to 2-color each connected component, including the trivial no-edge case.
Explicitly identifies the task as coloring nodes and checking bipartiteness.
Builds an adjacency list and assigns alternating colors through BFS.
Uses a color array and graph traversal to enforce alternating endpoint assignments.
